scientificAndNumericalReview: The arithmetic supports the empirical verdict in both languages. The mean accelerations over 0–6, 6–8 and 8–10 s are +1.333…, 0 and −2.0 m/s². The first three 2 s slopes are +1.6, +1.6 and +0.8 m/s², so the acceleration decreases in the last of those intervals. The five trapezoid areas are 3.2, 9.6, 14.4, 16.0 and 12.0 m, totaling 55.2 m. All velocities are nonnegative, so this area also gives distance traveled. The ideal fall time is 0.504818777 s and the nominal range is 4.03855022 m. The displayed 0.505 s and 4.04 m are correctly rounded. The defect requiring revision is the inference from the successful ball prediction and failed car prediction to the physical reason for that difference.
partOneToThreePreservationReview: The standalone 05cfd298 file matches the proposal in input.json and its supplied SHA-256. In both DE and EN, Materials 1–3, the numbered prompts 1–4 and the solution through part 4 match the canonical baseline. Scoring rows s1–s4 also match exactly. In particular, parts 1–3 retain their tasks, answers and 7, 6 and 7 marks. Part 4 retains 6 marks and its calculation, but the new printed answer and marking notes change what a marker can credit. The surrounding context adds the trials. The old 4-mark request for two model limits becomes a 10-mark empirical check with a new s5. partFourIntervalAndComparisonReview: The positive factors give the extrema 7.8 × (0.504818777 − 0.03) = 3.70358646 m and 8.2 × (0.504818777 + 0.03) = 4.38551397 m. Outward rounding gives [3.70, 4.39] m, width 0.69 m. This is an envelope from the prescribed input bounds. The ±0.03 s is applied to the model fall time in part 4. Material 4 supplies no individual flight times. Part 5 directs every learner to the printed envelope. In row order, the ball measurement intervals are [3.91, 4.01], [4.00, 4.10] and [4.06, 4.16] m, all contained in it. At the recorded speeds the ideal predictions are 3.98807, 4.03855 and 4.08903 m. Observed minus predicted is −0.02807, +0.01145 and +0.02097 m, confirming the stated 0.03 m bound. The car intervals are [2.93, 3.03], [3.01, 3.11] and [2.88, 2.98] m. The speed-specific residuals are −1.05855, −1.02903 and −1.05807 m. The highest allowed observation is 3.11 m, leaving 0.59 m to the printed lower bound. The car readings span 0.13 m and average 2.99 m, about 1.05 m short of the nominal prediction. At matched gate readings of 7.9, 8.0 and 8.1 m/s, the ball exceeds the car by 1.03, 1.07 and 1.05 m respectively. All six recorded speeds lie in [7.8, 8.2] m/s. That observation controls the prescribed comparison but does not measure the velocity of S at release.
pointParticleAndRotationObservableReview: The video quantity is the horizontal coordinate of S relative to the fixed ramp edge at the body's first ground contact. The side mark is stipulated to represent the car's centre of mass. The front touches first, but its horizontal coordinate is not the reading. The model sets x_S = 0 and vertical velocity to zero at launch and ends the motion after S drops the edge height h = 1.25 m. This defines a prediction for the named observable. Whether these start and end conditions represent the real events is part of the test. For an ideal sphere leaving horizontally above the edge of a level ramp, its centre starts at h + r and is at r at first contact with level ground. The equal radius offsets cancel, and its rotation leaves its contact height unchanged. This explains why a point representing S can work. The ratio 0.10/4.04 ≈ 2.5% is a scale check. It does not justify the key's statement that any point on the ball will do at ±0.05 m resolution. For the car, 4.2 m is comparable to the range, which makes contact geometry worth checking. In uniform gravity, rotation alone does not change the freely flying centre-of-mass trajectory for a given release state. Orientation can change the height of S at first contact, and support forces before release can change its initial state. Without drag, the observed distance is x_release + v_x,release × T, where T depends on release height, vertical velocity and centre height at contact. A horizontal approach across the edge and a gate reading just before it do not locate the loss of final support. If horizontal motion is intended to be imposed through that instant, the key's downward release velocity would itself relax that assumption. The wheelbase gives 2.6/8.0 = 0.325 s, approximately 0.33 s, comparable with the 0.505 s ideal flight time. It is a nominal axle-passage timescale. It supplies no measured release delay, pitch or correction to the range.
airResistanceBoundReview: Material 4 supplies an absolute bound of 0.05 m on the effect of drag on this same observable for each body. Its use is defensible for the compatibility decision. The outer ball measurement limits are 0.21 and 0.23 m inside the nearer ends of the printed interval. Allowing the full drag effect in either direction still leaves margins of 0.16 and 0.18 m. For the car, the most favorable correction leaves at least 0.59 − 0.05 = 0.54 m unexplained. Thus drag cannot reverse either classification or account for the car's shortfall on its own. Comparing 0.05 m only to the full 0.69 m width would miss the possibility of a reading near an endpoint. The bound equals a measurement half-width and exceeds every ball residual in magnitude, so it does not justify ignoring drag for a centimetre-level prediction. Its physical value is the team's supplied estimate. The trials do not independently determine drag, its sign or a drag law, and the estimate does not bound wheel–ramp contact forces.
passBoundaryAndMissingCoreReview: Let P = s1+s2+s3+s4, with maxima 7+6+7+6 = 26. Historically s5 had a maximum of 4 and a score r on it required P ≥ 18−r. For r = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 the respective boundaries were 18, 17, 16, 15, 14. Parts 1–3 alone offered 20, enough to pass at 18/30 (60%). Under the new rule, if any of K1–K5 is missing or wrong by the rubric, s5 is 1 when at least one core or extension contribution is correct and 0 otherwise. Even four correct cores and three correct extensions cannot lift this case above 1. With all five cores, s5 is 7 plus one for each of V1–V3 earned, hence 7, 8, 9 or 10. There are no authored levels 2–6 or fractional intermediate levels. At s5 = 0 or 1 the maximum total is 26 or 27. At s5 = 7, 8, 9 or 10, passing at 28/36 (77.78%) requires P ≥ 21, 20, 19 or 18 respectively. Equality passes and every lower unrounded score fails. These inequalities also cover fractional P. Omitting K1, K2, K3, K4 or K5 individually gives the same upper bound of 27 under faithful marking. No extension is compulsory for everyone, but P in [18,19), [19,20) or [20,21) requires three, two or one respectively. With s1 or s3 zero, passing requires at least 9 on s5. With s2 or s4 zero it requires at least 8. No two of s1–s4 can both be zero on a pass. K1 expressly permits naming the two supplied idealizations. Copying those names can satisfy K1 alongside independently earned K2 and K3. Copying an assumption alone satisfies neither justification. Copying the control alone earns zero on s4. An erroneous part 3 can earn method credit in part 4, but part 5 gives zero follow-through credit for conclusions drawn from a wrong interval. A reversed compatibility verdict loses K4 and caps the total at 27. For example, 20 on s1–s3, zero on s4 and a valid core gives 27, rising to 28 with one extension. That pass demonstrates use of the supplied control without demonstrating its independent derivation.
MODWholeGoalCoverageReview: The current MOD goal requires the learner to justify motion-model idealizations such as the point particle and friction neglect and identify limits of prediction. Part 5 genuinely asks for more than recall. K1 names the two idealizations, K2 asks for a scale comparison, K3 uses a supplied drag bound, and K4 requires two uncertainty-aware empirical judgments. The difficulty is K5's demand that the model reaches its limit for the car because the car is not small compared with the range. A scientifically justified answer can accept both empirical verdicts, identify extent and first-contact geometry as plausible, and decline to assign the discrepancy to size. The ball rolls freely after the launcher acts and the car approaches under its own drive. Matching edge, nominal height, g and pre-edge speed does not match the complete support-to-flight transition or the contact geometry. The combined prediction fails for the car in these trials. The data do not isolate which assumption failed. The question's 'could' and the acceptance of equivalent arguments support awarding this answer the core. The literal causal clause in K5 supports withholding it, which would turn even 26 other marks into a fail at 27. Conversely, a learner can repeat the size attribution, meet the remaining written clauses and pass with 21+7 while treating tipping as certain. The rubric withholds an extension for unsupported certainty but does not reliably remove the core. The numeric protection therefore does not establish truthful whole-MOD recognition on this exact file. MOD is the appropriate sole intended target after repair.
fullPreparationAndSourceStageReview: Traversing requires from horizontal projection (89a8cf15) and MOD (d6dc0e02) reaches exactly the 72 supplied goals, 15 Physics and 57 Mathematics. The Physics paths cover signed interval rates, graph areas, uniform and accelerated motion, motion laws, free fall, fall with air resistance, horizontal superposition, measurement uncertainty and error types. The Mathematics paths include units and scales, rational and decimal arithmetic and order, equations, functions, graph reading and areas. These support the mandatory calculations and bounded comparisons. The supplied HE Physics curriculum, p. 30, places motion diagrams, speed, acceleration, experimental free fall, point mass with neglected rotation and extent, and friction neglect in E.1. Horizontal projection, its experiment and its x–y representation are explicit in E.3 on p. 31. Pages 29–31 cover E1/E2 mechanics, with topics 1–3 binding across that phase. The content is appropriate for an own voluntary HE E1 LK offer once the actual projection and modeling preparation is available. The source does not establish that every first-semester learner has already had E.3 or that this particular examination is prescribed. No additional substantive prerequisite is needed. A unique vehicle release state cannot be recovered by teaching more mechanics from the same data. The learner analyzes the team's six results. Planning a discriminating measurement or a conditional stunt decision can earn optional credit. Neither activity records an experiment performed by this learner or a plotted experimental trajectory.
bilingualParityReview: DE and EN give the same observations, coordinate and contact event, gate location, drag and measurement bounds, control interval, required comparisons, numerical key and scoring levels. Both versions share the material discrepancy between a task asking what difference could account for the result and a mandatory criterion attributing failure to size. Both also make the same overstatement about the choice of point on the ball.

requiredCorrections: Align K2 and both solutions with the actual S-at-first-contact observable. Credit a justification using spherical geometry, the launch conditions and the empirical accuracy. Remove the claim that any point is interchangeable at the stated resolution.

Align K5 and both keys with the evidential demand in 5c. A learner who identifies the failed combined prediction, explains why extent or orientation could matter, and shows why the data cannot isolate the cause must be eligible for the full core. Size or a particular tipping mechanism cannot be required as an established cause.

Make the treatment of causal certainty consistent across the core and V1/V2. An unsupported attribution must not count as the required justification of a prediction limit merely because it repeats the key.

Scope K3's neglect of drag to the experimental decision for which the supplied bound is small enough. Use the margins to the decision boundaries and distinguish that conclusion from accuracy at the scale of an individual measurement.
unsupportedOrUnderdeterminedInferences: The car discrepancy has a measured direction and a bounded minimum size. Its allocation among release position, release velocity, effective drop, orientation and first-contact geometry is undetermined.

Front-first contact and the wheelbase do not establish a tipping angle, angular speed, centre-of-mass descent, duration of support, or magnitude or net sign of a rotational correction. At fixed other conditions a downward release velocity or a smaller drop can shorten flight. Other release changes can offset that effect.
The launcher acts before the ball rolls freely. There is no evidence of continued propulsion in flight. The differing approaches and support histories are possible confounders, not measured causes.

Three compatible ball trials support use at these speeds and this tolerance. They do not establish a universal size-to-range criterion. Three incompatible car trials do not establish a unique remedy or validate a stunt plan.
limits: The integration decision and empty direct-coverage recommendation apply to the exact file. The necessary repair concerns what the marking accepts. It can retain the two direct prerequisites, the agreed goal cut and 28-point threshold.

The pass proof assumes application of the authored s5 levels and comparison of the actual total with 28. The supplied objects provide no observation of a runtime grader, learner attempt, trial video or independent validation of the team's drag estimate.

The review covers content for the intended voluntary HE offer. Placement, deployment, other jurisdictions and actual learner readiness are outside its evidence. The scenario kind findings are conditional metadata judgments.

nativeOwnAssessmentSection4Review: Under the single-binary-result contract, the assessment pass must itself justify recognition of every claimed whole goal. Here the ordinary point total suffices to enforce the written s5 core. No extra gate, per-K runtime field or second learner result is needed. The control result also prevents a false empirical verdict from passing through follow-through credit. The remaining problem is semantic: the written core can accept an unsupported explanation and withhold credit for a scientifically better bounded conclusion. A marker's discretion to accept equivalent reasoning does not resolve contradictory mandatory wording. Withhold direct whole-MOD recognition for this exact identity pending revision. Prerequisite use, optional planning, author release, status labels and old 2b9e565f results supply none of the missing evidence.
